message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of $1.85 billion for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54% from a year earlier, and net income of $397 million, up 107.85%, in what the company called its second consecutive record quarter [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of $1,345 million, up 43.09%, and operating income of $458 million, up 86.18%, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of $501 million, up 21.60%, and operating income of $155 million, up 68.48%, taking total segment operating income to $613 million, up 81.36% [D1]. Management guided the fourth fiscal quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and to earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on 172 million diluted shares, which is approximately 37% revenue growth at the mid-point of the range [D1]. The quarter's strength is attributed to demand for testing linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure, which lifted orders well above expectations [D2].

The argument in the market is about conversion rather than demand, because management said the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago and that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, with the supply situation likely to be nonlinear [D3]. The shares fell 6.32% in the session of 2026-08-19 that followed the 2026-08-18 release, and the release dated 2026-05-19 was followed by a fall of 0.59% in the session of 2026-05-20, so the beat did not lift the price [D2]. The stock still trades at a trailing price to earnings multiple of 45.89 against a forward price to earnings multiple of 20.66, so the growth is already discounted [D5]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts this year will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar for future profitability [D4].

The plan is therefore to stay with the position while the next report confirms the guided range, with revenue of at least $1.93 billion and earnings per share of at least $3.34 keeping the case intact and revenue of at least $1.95 billion clearing the top of that range [D1]. A shortfall against $1.93 billion, or a gross margin below 65.87%, would confirm that supply rather than demand is the binding constraint, which is the signal to reduce [D1]. The close of 333.42 sits just above the immediate support high edge of 332.78, with the trend state marked as an uptrend and the relative strength index at 54.21, while immediate resistance sits at 366.41 [D2].
